mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 7 Series 740i engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 7 Series 740i engine replacement cost varies significantly by generation. E38 M62B44 engines cost £1,200-£2,200 used, £2,200-£3,800 reconditioned, and £3,000-£5,000 rebuilt. E65 N62B40 engines cost £1,800-£3,200 used, £2,800-£4,800 reconditioned, and £4,000-£6,000 rebuilt. G11 B58B30 engines cost £2,000-£3,800 used, £3,800-£6,000 reconditioned, and £5,000-£8,000 rebuilt. Supply & fit adds £780-£1,300 in specialist labour.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of valve stem seal failure in a BMW 740i (E65)?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common symptoms include blue or white smoke from the exhaust on cold startup, excessive oil consumption between services, and a strong smell of burning oil. The smoke typically clears after a few seconds but will return on the next cold start. Many E65 740i owners report this issue developing at 69,500 miles or earlier.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 7 Series 740i?

acceptedAnswer.text: This depends on the generation. For an E38 740i valued at £2,000-£8,000, a £3,000-£5,000 rebuilt engine may be borderline - carefully evaluate the car's overall condition. For an E65 740i valued at £2,000-£6,000, a valve stem seal repair (£1,800-£3,000) is often better value than a full rebuild. For a G11 740i valued at £18,000-£35,000, a rebuilt engine at £5,000-£8,000 represents 20-30% of the car's value and is financially viable.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 7 Series 740i engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical BMW 7 Series 740i engine replacement takes 2-5 days for supply and fit at a specialist garage. V8 engines (M62, N62) take longer due to the engine bay complexity, while straight-six engines (N55, B58) are more straightforward. Most specialists offer collection/delivery options nationwide with same-day dispatch available for in-stock engines.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the BMW 740i and 750i engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 740i has always been a V8 or straight-six engine, while the 750i has consistently been a V8. In the E38 generation, the 740i used a 4.0L or 4.4L V8 while the 750i used a 5.4L V12. In the E65 generation, the 740i used a 4.0L V8 while the 750i used a 4.8L V8. In the F01 and G11 generations, the 740i switched to a 3.0L straight-six while the 750i retained a 4.4L V8. The 750i generally offers more power and torque but carries higher replacement costs.

Reliability varies significantly by generation. The M62 V8 (E38) is known for timing chain guide failure. The N62 V8 (E65) is notorious for valve stem seal failure and oil consumption. The N55 straight-six (F01) is more reliable but has HPFP issues. The B58 straight-six (G11) is the most reliable of the bunch, with PCV valve failure being the main concern.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 7 Series 740i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 740i has been the heart of the 7 Series petrol range since the E38 generation launched in 1994. Over four generations, the 740i has evolved from a 4.0-litre V8 to a 4.4-litre V8, then to a 3.0-litre twin-turbo straight-six, and finally to the latest 3.0-litre B58 straight-six with mild-hybrid technology. Each generation brought more power, better efficiency, and its own set of engineering characteristics - and its own failure points.

milestones.description: M60B40, 4.0L V8, 286hp, introduced with the E38 740i
M62B44, 4.4L V8, 286hp, replaced M60B40 with improved VANOS system
M62TUB44, 4.4L V8, 286hp, facelift E38 with TU (technical update) engine
N62B40, 4.0L V8, 306hp, introduced with the E65 740i
N62B40TU, 4.0L V8, 306hp, updated Valvetronic and VANOS systems
N55B30, 3.0L twin-turbo straight-six, 326hp, introduced with the F01 740i
B58B30, 3.0L twin-turbo straight-six, 326hp, introduced with the G11 740i
B58B30 (updated), 3.0L twin-turbo straight-six, 340hp, G11 LCI update
B58B30 (G70), 3.0L straight-six with 48V mild-hybrid, 381hp, current generation

problems.h4: N62 Valve Stem Seal Failure - Why the E65 740i V8 Smokes on Startup
problems.rootCause: The N62 engine's valve stem seals degrade over time, allowing oil to leak into the combustion chambers. This causes blue/white smoke on startup (particularly after the car has been sitting) and excessive oil consumption. Many owners report this fault developing at 69,500 miles or earlier.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace all valve stem seals using specialist tooling (engine remains in car)
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early before catalytic converter damage

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded valve seals, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: The right call if valve seal failure has caused secondary damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical E65 740i currently values between £2,000 and £6,000 depending on condition and mileage. For sub-£4,000 examples, a valve stem seal repair at £1,800-£3,000 represents 45-75% of the car's value - careful evaluation is needed. For £4,000+ examples in good condition, the repair is justifiable.
problems.recommendation: If your E65 740i is smoking on startup but otherwise runs well, the specialist valve stem seal replacement (£1,800-£3,000) is the most cost-effective solution. A full engine replacement is rarely necessary unless the valve seal failure has caused catalytic converter or secondary damage.

problems.h4: M62 Timing Chain Guide Failure - Why the E38 740i V8 Rattles
problems.rootCause: The M62 V8 uses plastic timing chain guides that can become brittle and shatter with age and heat cycles. When the guides fail, the timing chain can slip, causing catastrophic engine failure. A rattling noise from the front of the engine is the early warning sign.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, guides, tensioners, and VANOS components
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early before chain slip

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, rebuilt timing system, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Necessary if chain has slipped causing valve/piston damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical E38 740i currently values between £2,000 and £8,000 depending on condition, with well-maintained examples commanding a premium. For sub-£4,000 examples, a timing chain guide repair at £1,500-£2,500 may be borderline. For £4,000+ examples, the repair is justifiable, especially for low-mileage or well-preserved cars.
problems.recommendation: If you hear rattling from the front of the engine, have the timing chain tensioner inspected immediately - a £50-£100 inspection could save you thousands. A guide replacement at £1,500-£2,500 is much cheaper than a full engine replacement and addresses the root cause.

problems.h4: B58 PCV Valve Failure - Why the G11 740i Misfires
problems.rootCause: The B58 engine's PCV (positive crankcase ventilation) valve can fail, causing a vacuum leak that leads to rough idle, misfires, and oil in the intake tract. This issue is particularly common on cars with upgraded turbos.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace PCV valve, clean intake, reset adaptations
Supply & fit, upgraded PCV system, 12-month warranty

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical G11 740i currently values between £18,000 and £35,000. A PCV valve replacement at £400-£800 is negligible relative to the car's value. A full engine replacement at £5,000-£8,000 represents 20-30% of the vehicle's value - well within the "safe" threshold.
problems.recommendation: If your G11 740i is misfiring or idling roughly, have the PCV valve checked first. The B58 is generally a reliable engine, and a PCV valve replacement is a straightforward fix that addresses the most common failure point.
